title: ICE Fatally Shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston; Witnesses Contradict DHS Account
excerpt: An ICE officer shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican national driving a construction crew to a job site in Houston. Passengers in the van denied that Salgado Araujo posed a threat to agents, directly contradicting the agency's self-defense claim.
content:
On July 7, 2026, an ICE officer shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican national, in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood as he drove a work crew to a construction site. ICE claimed Salgado Araujo "rammed" an agency vehicle and attempted to run over an officer, but at least two passengers in the van told their attorney that no agent was ever directly in front of the vehicle and that the shots came from the sides—not the front—contradicting the official account.

Salgado Araujo was confirmed to not be the target of the immigration operation; DHS said agents believed he resembled someone they were looking for. The shooting agents were not wearing body cameras. The incident is at least the eighth shooting death during the second Trump administration's immigration enforcement campaign and sparked immediate protests in Houston.

  • ICE said Salgado Araujo "weaponized" his vehicle; witnesses and family disputed this.
  • No body cameras were worn by the agents involved.
  • Hundreds marched in downtown Houston demanding an independent investigation and release of the witnesses from detention.
  • A federal judge later ordered that a key witness could not be deported while the investigation was ongoing.
"They confirmed that at no point was there ever an ICE agent directly in front of the vehicle. They also confirmed that the shots came from the sides, not from the front, which is inconsistent with the ICE statement." — Attorney Hugo Balderas, representing two passengers
